speaker: presidenta
text: Good afternoon, the Vice-President and I welcome you to our press conference.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council today decided to keep the three key ECB interest rates unchanged.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: While the incoming information has been broadly consistent with our previous assessment of the inflation outlook, the upside risks to inflation and the downside risks to growth have intensified.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are committed to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilises at our two per cent target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The war in the Middle East has led to a sharp increase in energy prices, pushing up inflation and weighing on economic sentiment.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The implications of the war for medium-term inflation and economic activity will depend on the intensity and duration of the energy price shock and the scale of its indirect and second-round effects.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The longer the war continues and the longer energy prices remain high, the stronger is the likely impact on broader inflation and the economy.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We remain well positioned to navigate the current uncertainty.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The euro area entered this period of surging energy prices with inflation at around our two per cent target, and the economy has shown resilience over recent quarters.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored, although inflation expectations over shorter horizons have moved up significantly.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will closely monitor the situation and follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In particular, our interest rate decisions will be based on our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, as well as the dynamics of underlying inflation and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are not pre-committing to a particular rate path.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The decisions taken today are set out in a press release available on our website.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I will now outline in more detail how we see the economy and inflation developing and will then explain our assessment of financial and monetary conditions.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The euro area economy was showing some momentum when the current turbulence started.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Real GDP grew by 0.1 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, according to Eurostat’s preliminary flash estimate.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Domestic demand remains the main driver of growth, supported by a resilient labour market.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: However, the economic outlook is highly uncertain and will depend on how long the war in the Middle East lasts and how strongly it affects energy and other commodity markets, as well as global supply chains.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The incoming information suggests that the conflict is weighing on economic activity.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Surveys point to slowing growth, and consumers and businesses have become less confident about the future since the war began.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Longer delivery times and rising input prices suggest supply chains are coming under pressure.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Looking ahead, high energy costs are expected to continue to weigh on real incomes, making households and firms more reluctant to consume and invest.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: While unemployment remained close to historical lows in March, at 6.2 per cent, labour demand has cooled further.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: At the same time, households are still benefiting from a solid financial position, and investment should continue to be underpinned by governments spending more on defence and infrastructure and by firms increasingly investing in new digital technologies.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This favourable starting point provides some cushioning against the fallout from the war.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council highlights the urgent need to strengthen the euro area economy while maintaining sound public finances.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Fiscal responses to the energy price shock should be temporary, targeted and tailored.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Reforms to enhance the euro area’s growth potential and accelerate the energy transition to reduce reliance on fossil fuels are more vital than ever.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Completing the savings and investments union is key to funding innovation, supporting the green and digital transitions and improving productivity.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The digital euro and tokenised wholesale central bank money will enhance Europe’s strategic autonomy, competitiveness and financial integration, and will boost innovation in payments.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It is thus essential to swiftly adopt the Regulation on the establishment of the digital euro.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Simplifying and harmonising rules across the EU’s Single Market will help European firms grow faster.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation rose to 3.0 per cent in April, from 2.6 per cent in March and 1.9 per cent in February.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The rise has been driven by surging energy prices caused by the war in the Middle East.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Energy price inflation jumped to 10.9 per cent in April, after 5.1 per cent in March.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Food price inflation edged up to 2.5 per cent in April.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation excluding energy and food decreased to 2.2 per cent, from 2.3 per cent in March, reflecting a fall in services inflation, which declined to 3.0 per cent, from 3.2 per cent in March.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Goods inflation went up to 0.8 per cent, from 0.5 per cent in March.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Indicators of underlying inflation have changed little over recent months.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: For now, the ECB’s wage tracker and surveys on wage expectations continue to indicate easing labour costs in the course of 2026.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: At the same time, surveys indicate an increase in other cost components and in selling price expectations.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation expectations have moved up significantly over shorter horizons.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Most measures of longer-term inflation expectations stand at around 2 per cent, supporting the stabilisation of inflation around target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The increase in energy prices will keep inflation well above 2 per cent in the near term.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: As the period of high energy prices extends, the likely impact on broader inflation through indirect and second-round effects intensifies.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We will therefore closely monitor the size and persistence of the energy price surge, and how it feeds through to price and wage-setting, inflation expectations, and overall economic dynamics.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: The war in the Middle East remains a downside risk to the euro area economy, adding to the volatile global policy environment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Prolonged disruption of the supply of energy could increase energy prices further and for longer than currently expected.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: These factors would erode incomes and make firms and households more reluctant to invest and spend.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The drag on growth would intensify if the closure of major shipping routes were to cause acute shortages of key inputs that forced euro area firms to curtail output.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: A worsening of global financial market sentiment could further dampen demand.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Additional frictions in international trade could exacerbate supply chain disruptions, reduce exports and weaken consumption and investment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Other geopolitical tensions, in particular Russia’s unjustified war against Ukraine, remain a major source of uncertainty.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: By contrast, growth could turn out to be higher if the economy proved to be more adaptable to the disruption caused by the war in the Middle East or if the conflict were resolved more quickly than currently expected.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Moreover, planned defence and infrastructure spending, reforms to enhance productivity, and euro area firms adopting new technologies may drive up growth by more than expected.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: New trade agreements and a deeper integration of the Single Market could also boost growth beyond current expectations.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: If energy prices were to rise by more and for longer than currently expected, euro area inflation would increase further.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: This could be reinforced and become more persistent if higher energy prices were to spill over by more than expected to other prices and to wages, if longer-term inflation expectations were to rise in response, or if global supply chains were disrupted more broadly.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Ongoing trade tensions could also give rise to more fragmented global supply chains, curtail the supply of critical raw materials and worsen capacity constraints in the euro area economy.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: By contrast, inflation could turn out to be lower if the economic effects of the war in the Middle East proved to be more short-lived than currently expected or if indirect and second-round effects proved less pronounced.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: More volatile and risk-averse financial markets could weigh on demand and thereby lower inflation as well.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: The war in the Middle East has caused significant volatility in global financial markets.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Overall financial conditions remain tighter than before the war.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The cost of issuing market-based debt rose to 3.9 per cent in March, from 3.5 per cent in February.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Bank lending rates for firms – based on data recorded prior to the war – edged down to 3.5 per cent in February, while mortgage rates remained at 3.4 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The annual growth rate of bank lending to firms increased to 3.2 per cent in March, from 3.0 per cent in February, while the growth rate of corporate bond issuance fell to 3.9 per cent, from 4.5 per cent in February.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Credit standards for loans to firms tightened in the first quarter, as reported in our latest bank lending survey for the euro area.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This tightening was due to banks becoming more concerned about the economic risks faced by their customers.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Demand for loans to firms decreased slightly in the first quarter, especially for fixed investment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Mortgage lending grew by 3.0 per cent in March, after 3.1 per cent in February, amid a small tightening in credit standards and unchanged demand.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council today decided to keep the three key ECB interest rates unchanged.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are committed to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilises at our two per cent target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Our interest rate decisions will be based on our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, as well as the dynamics of underlying inflation and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are not pre-committing to a particular rate path.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In any case, we stand ready to adjust all of our instruments within our mandate to ensure that inflation stabilises sustainably at our medium-term target and to preserve the smooth functioning of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are now ready to take your questions.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I think we would all wish that there was a quick end to the war.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But looking at our monetary policy and the decision that we made today, we decided to keep the three interest rates unchanged.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And to address your questions, I'm not going to tell you whether we are closer to the baseline, or scenario one, or scenario two, because I think that what we have debated over the course of yesterday and today with the Governing Council, is where are we relative to the baseline?
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And the conclusion is that we are certainly moving away from the baseline.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Where to exactly, at what point in between baseline and other scenarios is, I'm not sure, the most relevant assessment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are moving away from the baseline, and what is critically important is the impact that energy prices will have.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I said last time in March that it would be a question of the duration, the depth, and the propagation, and this is clearly what we need to better assess.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: If I was to summarise for you what we decided today, I would say that we made an informed decision on the basis of yet insufficient information.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So why do I say it's an informed decision?
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It's because we debated, at length and in depth, various options.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We debated the decision that we have unanimously taken today, but we also debated, at length and in depth, a decision to possibly hike.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So that was debated amongst all governors, and I'm sure that you will meet some governors who will argue both sides, or maybe one side, of both proposals.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So it was really a deeply-discussed monetary policy stance, of which the outcome was a unanimous decision to leave the three interest rates unchanged.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And why I'm saying that it's an informed decision based on insufficient information; it is caused by the fact that, while the hard data is broadly in line with our projection and what we discussed here back in March, but there is such uncertainty that we need to understand and revisit all of that at our next monetary policy meeting.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And we believe that, given the position we are in, we are saying in the monetary policy statement that we started from a good position, we were well-positioned to navigate.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So, given that position, we believe that these six weeks will be the right time to assess the development, to understand in particular the outcome, possibly, of the conflict, or if there is no outcome – that in and of itself will be informative – in order to make an informed decision on verified and revisited information that we will receive in the next six weeks.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: That's the clearest way – I hope it was clear – that I can describe the really good discussions that we had both yesterday and today.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Thank you for your two questions.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: On the first one, we take the view that it's quite popular to talk about stagflation, and it flags a lot of anxiety and all the rest of it.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I think we have determined that stagflation is the right characterization of what happened in the 1970s, but from our perspective, we think that it's better to park it in the 1970s, given the facts that we have at the moment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You know, it's a completely different situation.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In the 1970s, you had inflation continuing, continuing, continuing at a sort of sustainable and solid pace.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You had very high unemployment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You had a monetary and fiscal framework that had nothing to do with what we have at the moment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So, we don't apply stagflation, that flashy term, to the circumstances that we have because we really think that it's associated with the 1970s situation.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: On the tools, you know, we have a whole series of tools in our toolbox, but certainly from our perspective, and given the data that we have and the kind of shock that we're facing, we believe that the interest rates are still the best tool that we can use and that we have debated in the course of yesterday and today.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: I'm so pleased that you mentioned the reaction function because we spend quite a lot of time working it out, finding consensus around the reaction function, and as you know, because you're a frequent reader and observer of what we do, the reaction function has been very clearly spelt out in our strategy review that we published in 2025, and that I have tried to elaborate on and that I have tried to apply to the current circumstances in both my speeches to the Watchers and in Berlin last week.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I have for myself three anchors of what our reaction function is.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So first of all, to remind you, the target is 2 per cent medium term, number one.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Number two, symmetry.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We discussed that today and we reaffirmed it.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Number three, our reaction will depend on the type of deviation from target that we observe.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Is it large and sustainable?
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In that case – obviously, we have calibrated in our strategy review and in those two speeches that I have committed in the last few days – in that case, we have a forceful or persistent reaction to return inflation to our target of 2 per cent medium-term.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: That's our reaction function.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And the data and the process that we use in order to deliver on that reaction function is what you see: monetary policy statement after monetary policy statement, which is the inflation outlook with the risks associated to it, and as you will have seen in the monetary policy statement, we have a strong chapter on both risks to growth and risk to inflation.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: That's how we bring in the risk to growth, to your point.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We also look at underlying inflation and we look at the dynamics of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So, the reaction function, the process and the tools that we use in order to apply that reaction function.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And, of course, we look at the specificity of what we are going through, and that's where you will find more details in both my speech to the Watchers – you are one of them, I'm sure – and my speech in Berlin to the bankers.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And I think I tried in those two documents, particularly the latter, to really apply the reaction function and the tools to the circumstances through which we're going, in particular a supply shock, a strong supply shock, a negative one of course, and to see whether we are going to use one or the other approach in order to deliver on our target of 2 per cent in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You asked me about the scenarios.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We constantly monitor.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We constantly take in new data, hard data, soft data, survey results from all sorts of perspectives and we verify and we adjust and we take stock of all that.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In June, six weeks from now, you will be receiving not only the projections that our staff will produce, but you will also see the scenarios as revised and as updated as a result of the circumstances.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So, I'll take the first question and then I'll give the floor to the Vice-President.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We still have abundance of liquidity.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: You mentioned 2.6 – I think it’s a little down from that number, but it's a significant amount of excess liquidity in the system.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So, there is no shortage of liquidity and, as you know, we have a mechanism that works on the basis of access to liquidity: it's a fixed interest rate, full allotment, good collateral, it's working well and we're not seeing any tension in that respect.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Did we discuss new tools?
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The answer is no, because what we discussed, and it was on the agenda yesterday, we discussed the timetable and the methodology that will be adopted in-house by staff, as well as within the Eurosystem, bringing all the committees in the loop to calibrate our operational framework to make sure that it is fit for purpose and that it is good from a financial stability point of view, as well as from a proper functioning of the providing of liquidity, which is obviously one of the missions that we have.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: With that, I'll turn the floor over to you, my dear Luis.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: Thank you very much, President, and good afternoon to everyone.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: Well, we have no doubts about the liquidity position and the capital position of the European banks.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: The European banks are resilient and we do not believe that liquidity or capital is any sort of limitation for lending, and this is something that we have analysed quite in detail.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: So I would say that we are confident that they have enough liquidity, that they have enough capital, and that they are meeting the purpose that we wanted to deliver, that is, that banks meet the needs and the financial needs of families, households and corporates.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: You referred to private credit.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: Well, we are going to dedicate a full chapter of our Financial Stability Review to private credit.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: It is something that is catching the eye of markets because of some liquidity issues.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: Private credit is a totally different animal in comparison with the banks in terms of oversight, in terms of the way that they function.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: And we are going to analyse interlinkages between private credit and other players as insurance companies, as the banks, and with private equity.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: And I think that you will have a full explanation of our approach and our assessment of the potential financial stability risks posed by private credit in our financial stability review that is going to be published in three weeks.

speaker: presidenta
text: We around the table of the Governing Council and the staff of the ECB and the Eurosystem are very attentive to our history.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We don't have a long history, but we are paying attention to what has been done in the past.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And you might argue that we, learning from history, will want to stay away from the risk of being too early – that's your reference to 2011 and the risk of being a little bit too late and that's what some of you would characterise for 2022.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I would like to debate that forever, of course, but that's where we are.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are going to be very attentive to the data, very attentive to the inflation expectations, very attentive to the supply chain disruptions, very much looking into the depth of the wage agreements and the collective agreements that will be negotiated in the near future, attentive to selling prices.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I mean, there is a whole range of data that we will be paying attention to in the next few weeks, and there will be plenty of it coming in the next few weeks, to be certain that from the good position we are in, we make the right decision, because our determination is to bring inflation to 2 per cent in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And that, you know, there is an ocean of uncertainty.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Things might change, for the good or for the bad, but one thing is certain: we are determined to return inflation to 2 per cent in the medium term.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: My dear Vice-President.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: Thank you, President.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: If you look at our reply, the reply of the Eurosystem to the consultation process that was launched by the European Commission that we published a couple of weeks ago, you will realise that the main message that is embedded in that report is that we are in favour of a single jurisdiction for the European banks with free flow of capital and liquidity.
label: neutral

speaker: vicepresidente
text: And I think that, referring to the deal that you have indicated, that you have alluded to, I think that this principle applies very clearly.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I think with all due respect to my predecessors, including my dear friend Jean-Claude, I try not to be exceedingly coded, so it's not because I add one adverb or one adjective here or there that is going to mean necessarily this or that.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But on the basis of, number one, the hard data that we are getting, on the basis of the worsening of our risk assessment, you will have noted that the nice word “tilted” has been removed and that we are not saying long-term versus short-term, we are looking throughout the period and considered that risk is to the downside for growth and to the upside for inflation.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So, on the basis of that and in view of the uncertainty that we have around, we are bound to revisit the situation on the basis of the data, the projection, the sensitivity analysis, the updated scenarios, and then we will take a decision.

text: I think, directionally, I know where we're heading.

speaker: presidenta
text: But we shall see.

text: There might be massive changes taking place.

text: I think I dealt with stagflation, because that's really something that I park in the 1970s, and given the projection that we have for March, 0.9 per cent growth followed by 1.3 [per cent], followed by 1.4 [per cent], I wouldn't call that stagnation, sorry.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It's lower growth, granted, in 2026, but we're not in stagnation, let alone recession.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Now, you can imagine scenarios where we are heading towards those situations but this is not what we are seeing for the moment.

text: Thank you for your first question and thank you for reminding everyone that in the design of our baseline and of our two scenarios, one adverse, one severe, we had in those situations two rate hikes which were embedded in bothbaseline andscenarios, given the cut-off date that we took.

speaker: presidenta
text: And as you know, this has changed over the course of time.

text: It goes from two to one, to three, but two was certainly the one.

text: And that means that our reaction function is well understood, right?

speaker: presidenta
text: That's point number one.

speaker: presidenta
text: Point number two, we are not seeing second-round effects.
